topic: A local model infers what a toy network was trained to do by reading its pasted weights
title: Your Laptop Model Can Read Another Network's Mind
description: We pasted the weights of a 17,253-parameter toy network into a local Qwen 27B, and it worked out the game the network plays. It read the pasted weights, never its own. Run it tonight: ollama run qwen3.8:27b with a long context. The prompt is at github.com/RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs.
hook_text: Your laptop model reads another mind
hook_candidates: Your laptop model can read another network's mind.
Seventeen thousand numbers. It named the game.
Forty-six minutes. Your laptop read a neural net.
Seventeen gigabytes. It reads weights, not words.
Qwen 3.8 read raw weights and guessed the game.
Three of four games. From numbers alone.
You downloaded a model. It reads other minds.
Seventeen thousand weights in. Pac-Man out.
Your model file can read its own kind.
No calculator. It still named the game.
narration_full: Your laptop model can read another network's mind. Seventeen thousand two hundred fifty-three parameters, and it names the game. Those parameters are not its own. You paste a toy network's weights, its numbers, into the chat as text. The numbers land. One number alone says nothing. Together they are clues: rows become cells, cells become a grid. Asked what it does, the model answers: Pac-Man. That is a big model reading a small network's weights. It never read its own. The repo has the prompts waiting. Tonight your machine reads a mind, and knows its limits.

notes_for_review: Worked example carried as the Pac-Man run; turns named by what changes: the numbers land (s02), rows become cells (s03), the answer names the game (s04). Correction delivered twice: s02 "not its own" and s04 "It never read its own". Analogy is null on purpose: no signature vehicle fits weight-reading, and the mechanism is stated plainly instead. Key numbers spent: two (seventeen thousand two hundred fifty-three parameters; twenty-seven-billion-parameter tag), one per sentence. The 17,253 figure is spoken only in s01; its reappearance on the final frame is the deliberate loop-anchor recall. Repo slug is on screen; narration says "RikiyaT's repo". One generic scene allowed and used (s03); all others carry a number or named entity. Total 110 words, est 37.9 s, inside the classic sweet band. Payoff sentence is last; nothing follows it.
